summary: The 17 tasks are buildable under the stated constraints: file lists sit inside group globs, no file is owned twice, the dependency graph is acyclic and gives each test task the backend code it needs, the 7 operations come from exactly two backend tasks, all 24 criteria map to exactly one test task, and nothing needs an uninstalled library. Findings concern thin backend verification and size margins.

criteria.description: Each task respects the 3-file and under-150-line budget and its group globs
criteria.notes: Max 3 files per task; backend files under app/** or migrations/**, tests under tests/**, no backend task touches tests; estLines 70-130; be-migrations and the larger test tasks are tight (P-2).

criteria.description: Dependency order is correct and acyclic, test tasks depend on the right backend tasks
criteria.notes: be-schemas after be-security, be-deps after core/models/security, routes after deps and schemas, be-app after both routers; te-fixtures after be-app and every conftest user after te-fixtures; te-security after be-security; te-migration after be-migrations and be-models.

criteria.description: Every operation is provided by exactly one backend task
criteria.notes: be-auth-routes provides registerUser, loginUser, logoutUser; be-task-routes provides listTasks, createTask, getTask, updateTask; no overlap, none missing.

criteria.description: Every PRD criterion is covered by a test task
criteria.notes: AC-1..AC-24 each appear exactly once in test-task criteria; the verify commands of AC-21..AC-24 name test files that te-fixtures, te-security, te-session and te-migration create (AC-22 persistence gap noted in P-4).

criteria.description: Every verification command is plausible to pass as written
criteria.notes: ruff 0.16.9 with --no-cache --select E,F --line-length 100 on listed files, and python -m pytest <file> -q for test tasks, all runnable from the repo root with the installed tools; weakness of the lint-only backend checks is P-1.

criteria.description: Nothing requires a library that is not installed
criteria.notes: Only fastapi, starlette, pydantic, sqlalchemy, alembic, httpx (TestClient), pytest and stdlib hashlib.scrypt, hmac, secrets are used; email-validator, jwt, bcrypt, argon2 deliberately avoided.

criteria.description: Estimates are consistent with the plan and config limits
criteria.notes: 9 backend and 8 test tasks match the counts; summed 90-260 minutes fits maxRuntimeMinutes 480; labelled uncalibrated.

findings.title: Backend verification is lint-only, behavior is first checked by tasks that cannot fix it
findings.detail: Every be-* task verifies only with ruff (plan.json tasks[].verification.command), although their acceptance criteria describe behavior. An import error or mapping error in app/models.py passes its task and surfaces later in a te-* task, whose group cannot edit app/**, so retries (maxTaskRetries 2) are wasted on the wrong group.
findings.recommendation: Chain an import check onto the backend commands, e.g. 'ruff check ... && python -c "import app.models"' and for be-app 'DATABASE_URL=sqlite:// python -c "import app.main"' (in-memory URL keeps it independent of the sandbox temp directory).

findings.title: Size margins are thin on be-migrations and the larger test tasks
findings.detail: be-migrations has 3 files (env.py, script.py.mako, 0001_initial.py) with estLines 110; a normal alembic env.py with offline and online modes, a 3-table revision with indexes and downgrade and the template come to roughly 140-150 lines against the under-150 budget. te-read-update, te-session and te-bola estimate 130 and cover 4 or 5 criteria with many 422 cases.
findings.recommendation: Tell be-migrations to write online mode only and a minimal template; tell the test tasks to parametrize 422 cases and keep helpers in conftest; otherwise split be-migrations into env+template and revision.

findings.title: Test tasks do not list prd.json, access-matrix.json or fixtures.json as inputs
findings.detail: te-* inputs are only openapi.json, db-schema.json and spec.md, although te-bola and the register/session tests need the AC text, the access matrix and the fixture accounts (user, other_user, admin@example.com). Also .eccode/artifacts, .eccode/design and contracts are currently untracked in git, and a group sees only HEAD.
findings.recommendation: Add the three inputs to the test tasks and make sure contracts/** and spec.md are committed before the build starts.

findings.title: No test owns the stored-not-plaintext half of AC-22
findings.detail: AC-22 requires that no plaintext password is persisted. te-security depends only on be-security and tests helpers; te-register (which has a client and database) lists only 'no password or hash field appears in any response'. No acceptance criterion reads users.password_hash from the database.
findings.recommendation: Add to te-register: after registering, the stored password_hash starts with 'scrypt$', differs per user for equal passwords and does not contain the plaintext.

findings.title: be-migrations must work without alembic.ini
findings.detail: brief.md says alembic.ini is added later by the orchestrator, while te-migration depends on be-migrations and runs before that. Its acceptance criteria do not require env.py to work with a programmatic Config (config_file_name None), so an unguarded fileConfig call would fail the test task.
findings.recommendation: Add to be-migrations acceptance: env.py runs with a programmatic Config and no ini file; te-migration builds Config in code and sets script_location and sqlalchemy.url.

findings.title: Estimates are uncalibrated
findings.detail: estimates.json is labelled agent-estimate-uncalibrated; token ranges (270k-750k) cannot be checked against maxCostUsd 25 in .eccode/config.json.
findings.recommendation: No change needed; recalibrate after this run.
